boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Ten named destinations along downtown Denton corridors in the practical off-campus orbit of UNT.

cards.title: See the 1896 courthouse museum
cards.subtitle: Hickory Street corridor — 110 W Hickory St
cards.notes: Walk the Hickory Street corridor to the museum, then use its posted exhibits and historic courtroom as a focused downtown history stop.
cards.short_summary: A county museum inside Denton’s restored 1896 courthouse.
cards.evidence_claim: Denton County identifies the 1896 building at 110 W Hickory Street as home to the Courthouse-on-the-Square Museum and states that admission is free.
cards.access_notes: Posted hours: Monday–Friday 10 a.m.–4 p.m.; Saturday 11 a.m.–3 p.m.; closed Sunday and major holiday weekends.

cards.title: Check the Theatre Denton program
cards.subtitle: Hickory Street corridor — 214 W Hickory St
cards.notes: On the Hickory Street corridor, check the current Theatre Denton schedule and choose a stage production or class that fits your visit.
cards.short_summary: A restored downtown theater used for year-round community productions.
cards.evidence_claim: Discover Denton states that Campus Theatre at 214 W Hickory Street hosts year-round productions from Denton Community Theatre and Music Theatre of Denton.
cards.access_notes: Check Theatre Denton’s current event listing before going; performances and classes may require registration or tickets.

cards.title: Look for gallery programming
cards.subtitle: Hickory Street corridor — 400 E Hickory St
cards.notes: Follow Hickory Street east to the arts center and consult its current listings for exhibitions, gallery visits, or Festival Hall events.
cards.short_summary: A former steam power plant repurposed for galleries and arts space.
cards.evidence_claim: Discover Denton lists the Patterson-Appleton Arts Center at 400 E Hickory Street and describes two galleries, an art studio, rehearsal hall, sculpture garden, and Festival Hall.
cards.access_notes: Exhibition and event access varies; consult the center’s current calendar before visiting.

cards.title: Browse the former Opera House
cards.subtitle: Locust Street corridor — 200 N Locust St
cards.notes: Use the Locust Street corridor for a three-floor browse of used books and recorded media; allow time to explore the changing stock.
cards.short_summary: A used-media shop in Denton’s purple former Opera House.
cards.evidence_claim: Discover Denton lists Recycled Books at 200 N Locust Street in a three-floor, 17,000-square-foot former Opera House with books and recorded media.
cards.access_notes: Retail browsing is available at the listed location; purchases are optional but inventory changes.

cards.title: Find a downtown UNT exhibition
cards.subtitle: Elm Street corridor — 207 N Elm St, Suite 101
cards.notes: Head along Elm Street to check UNT CoLab’s current calendar for exhibitions, concerts, poetry readings, and other public programming.
cards.short_summary: UNT’s downtown venue for exhibitions and community-facing arts events.
cards.evidence_claim: UNT states that UNT CoLab presents exhibitions, concerts, poetry readings, and more in downtown Denton; UNT lists the venue at 207 N Elm Street, Suite 101.
cards.source_title: We Are Part of the Community | University of North Texas
cards.access_notes: Programming changes by date; use UNT CoLab’s event calendar to confirm a specific public event.

cards.title: Try a bouldering session
cards.subtitle: Oak Street corridor — 220 W Oak St
cards.notes: On the Oak Street corridor, review Movement’s current entry options and choose a bouldering or fitness session appropriate to your experience.
cards.short_summary: A downtown bouldering gym in a former mattress factory.
cards.evidence_claim: Discover Denton lists Movement Climbing + Fitness at 220 W Oak Street and describes climbing terrain, a yoga studio, co-working spaces, and training areas.
cards.access_notes: Climbing and fitness access is a paid facility service; confirm waivers, entry options, and session details directly with the gym.

cards.title: Use the central library services
cards.subtitle: Oakland Street corridor — 502 Oakland St
cards.notes: Take Oakland Street to the central library for a quiet work stop, public computers, Wi-Fi, printing, scanning, or a study room.
cards.short_summary: Denton’s central public library with study and digital-access services.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Denton lists Emily Fowler Central Library at 502 Oakland Street with public computers, Wi-Fi, study and meeting rooms, printing, and scanning services.
cards.access_notes: Posted hours include Tuesday and Thursday until 9 p.m.; room use and borrowing may have separate requirements.

cards.title: Plan a Saturday market visit
cards.subtitle: Mulberry Street corridor — 317 W Mulberry St
cards.notes: Use Mulberry Street on a Saturday in season to walk the producer-only market, hear live music, and meet local farmers and makers.
cards.short_summary: A seasonal Saturday market with local producers, makers, and food vendors.
cards.evidence_claim: Discover Denton states that Denton Community Market operates at 317 W Mulberry Street on Saturdays, April through November, with local farmers, makers, food trucks, live music, and kids activities.
cards.source_title: Farmer's Markets and U-Picks | Denton, TX
cards.access_notes: Seasonal schedule listed as Saturdays, April–November, 9 a.m.–1 p.m.; vendor purchases are optional.

cards.title: Learn the Quakertown story
cards.subtitle: Mulberry Street corridor — 317 W Mulberry St
cards.notes: At the Mulberry Street historical park, use the museum’s materials to learn about Quakertown and Denton County African American families.
cards.short_summary: A museum in the relocated Quakertown House at the county historical park.
cards.evidence_claim: Discover Denton states that the Denton County African American Museum at 317 W Mulberry Street chronicles Denton County African American families and the Quakertown experience.
cards.access_notes: Located within Denton County Historical Park; confirm museum availability and tour details before visiting.

cards.title: Walk the historical-park grounds
cards.subtitle: Mulberry Street corridor — 317 W Mulberry St
cards.notes: Walk the Mulberry Street grounds and look for the Bayless-Selby and Quakertown house museums; request a guided tour if you want context.
cards.short_summary: A county historical park with house museums and community events.
cards.evidence_claim: Denton County lists the Historical Park at 317 W Mulberry Street as home to the Bayless-Selby House and Quakertown House museums and says admission is free.
cards.access_notes: Posted hours: Wednesday–Saturday, 10 a.m.–2 p.m.; the county states admission is free and guided tours are available on request.
